prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a clear FOUR-PANEL mechanical action study of the inverse combination of the EXACT allied giant in reference 1. This is a separate narrative action sheet, not its normal hero portrait. Sophisticated Japanese mechanical illustration, the same mature detailed linework, armor volume, colors and restrained painted finish as the references.

References:
1 = exact 900-meter Wanjidian body to preserve in every panel. Navy upper arm and gray-red forearm are anatomical RIGHT / viewer LEFT; damaged anatomical LEFT shoulder has the ivory/teal bridge-rescue ship Zhanqiao.
2 = the solo ships. TOP LEFT is the single museum ship; TOP RIGHT is Zhanqiao rescue ship; BOTTOM LEFT is Zhendeng maintenance cruiser with pipe arm; BOTTOM RIGHT is Zhefan outboard escort. Never interchange these identities.
3 = the actual armor-dock carrier, right-arm gunships, support carriers and thick shoulder-boom/clamp modules. These are the parts that move.
4 = hostile Tianqiong/cannon reference. In the final panel, show only a cropped section of that ENEMY'S large external gun cradle as the object being gripped; do not change Wanjidian into Tianqiong.

Layout: landscape sheet, four equally clear substantial vignettes in a 2 by 2 reading order, generous cream gutters, NO written labels, numbers, arrows, captions, logos or watermark. Each panel depicts ONE instance of the same allied giant and exactly ONE museum ship, hidden or visible according to the stage. This is four different moments, not four robots in one scene. Keep the same front/side three-quarter orientation and lighting across panels, with a faint Earth limb always toward the LOWER LEFT, so the Earth-side escape direction stays understandable. Do not invert the giant's right-arm colors between panels. The main torso, hips, armored legs and compact head remain continuous throughout; only the specified side-dock/chest covers are released.

TOP LEFT — TAKE THE WEIGHT, BEFORE RELEASE:
The giant is still in its closed-chest normal state from reference 1. Two small but credible independent navy/ivory utility towships have moved to the two ends of the substantial commercial side-dock/chest-cover assembly. Thick buffered tow cables are taut and clearly taking its weight. The small industrial yellow release locks are still engaged. The maintenance cruiser Zhendeng retracts its segmented coolant/service pipe arm near the anatomical left lower torso after isolating the connection. The museum ship remains INSIDE, only its existing tiny window/dome glimpse visible. Zhanqiao still supports the wounded left shoulder. Do not show the museum outside yet.

TOP RIGHT — RELEASE SIDE DOCK, THEN WITHDRAW CORE:
The two tugs now carry the real, heavy inhabited side-dock outer shell away toward lower-left Earth side. It is ONE coherent armor-and-harbor assembly, with large ivory/navy chest shell surfaces, tiny rectangular passenger windows, an entrance platform and small yellow latch housings. It is not a cloud of armor confetti and not a second museum ship. The released structural shell has moved far enough to open the escape route before the museum moves. The single familiar 150-meter museum ship, with blue glass dome, terraced galleries and orange entrance, slides HORIZONTALLY from the central cradle toward the Earth-side lower opening. It must fit visibly through the newly cleared opening, with free space around the hull: no clipping through closed breast armor. The main shoulder/hip structure remains thick and connected.

BOTTOM LEFT — A REAL VACANT CHEST, CORE SAFE BELOW:
Show the giant with its central museum cradle NOW EMPTY. A substantial clean through-opening exists in the chest where the single ship was, with visible dark depth and open space beyond. It is bounded by thick armored boxed structures, not thin scaffolding. Head, shoulders, spine connection, pelvis, both ship-arms and long armored legs remain identifiable from reference 1.
The ONE museum ship is completely outside and below on the Earth side, still horizontal. Zhanqiao has descended from the wounded shoulder and moved between the museum and the enemy direction, its twin buffered cables helping steady the museum. Zhendeng is a separate withdrawing armored repair hull with its pipe arm retracting; Zhefan remains outboard and provides cover rather than supporting mass. The detached side-dock assembly continues away with its two tugs in the distance. The central opening must be truly vacant, not filled with another glass dome or another copy of the museum. No giant's own gun grows out of this hole.

BOTTOM RIGHT — TWO SHOULDER BOX BEAMS TURN FORWARD AND CLAMP:
Keep the same empty-chested giant, with the two existing thick armored SHOULDER BOOMS from reference 3 rotating forward from their actual shoulder roots. These are heavy deep box beams with articulated roots and terminal industrial clamp jaws, not thin cables or ordinary fists. Both beam roots remain connected to the giant's surviving central chassis. Show the joints and armored load path clearly.
The two clamp jaws close around opposite sides of a massive EXTERNAL ENEMY CANNON ROTATING CRADLE, entering the panel from the upper-right/front. The enemy weapon is distinct from the allied giant; show a cropped section of the hostile cannon housing and rotation mount, with its long barrel extending out of the panel. Grip the rotating support FRAME near the gun root, not the muzzle. The original right-shoulder propulsion cradle remains mechanically locked at this stage; no premature detached beam floating unsupported.
The museum ship is still exactly one independent craft, near the lower part of the cleared chest passage heading diagonally toward the right side of the hostile gun cradle. It is not the cannon and not a torso part anymore. The gray-red right forearm and navy upper arm remain intact and visible lower on the giant; they do not become extra shoulder booms. Preserve a strong humanoid body even in this sacrificed-armor state.

Overall: mechanical action clarity through actual positions, intact physical masses and continuity, not arrows or text. Ships should retain their mother-sheet silhouettes. The museum is small relative to the 900-meter giant, not enlarged to fill the entire torso. Yellow locks are industrial small levers, never flower motifs. Zhefan is an independent red-gray long escort and carries no adjacent ship weight. Keep plated body mass and mature hero proportions throughout. No explosions that hide components, no magical melting, no random extra limbs, no duplicate museum in a single panel, no toy cartoon simplification, no flat infographic look. Fine technical drawing, deep occluded mechanisms, calm ivory/navy armor, gray-red right forearm, teal rescue ship accents, soft cream background and subtle pale Earth curve.

There is one maintenance ship, not two. Keep the one museum and one teal rescue ship below, with the rescue cables as drawn.

BOTTOM RIGHT panel — most important:
The TWO clamp beams must originate from the giant's TWO SHOULDERS. The current image makes them appear to originate from the upper and lower edges of the chest hole. Correct that wrong load path.
Open/rotate the relevant broad shoulder armor just enough to expose two thick rotary roots: one directly below the large VIEWER-LEFT shoulder cap, above the navy upper-arm hull, and one at the wounded VIEWER-RIGHT shoulder where the rescue ship has departed. Both roots must be visibly connected to the surviving shoulder girdle and central spine. FROM THESE TWO SHOULDER ROOTS, two deep plated BOX BEAMS extend FORWARD toward the enemy gun cradle on the right. The nearer beam may cross diagonally in front of part of the upper chest; the farther beam remains separately traceable behind it. Their distal heavy clamp jaws grip opposite sides of the enemy's large gun-rotation support FRAME. Pitch one beam slightly down and the other slightly up as necessary, but do not invent a beam rooted at the belly, sternum or bottom of the chest hole. Use the real boxed beam and industrial jaws from the lower-right of image 2. Ordinary arms and hands remain down and separate: navy upper arm/gray-red forearm on viewer left stays identifiable and is not the new clamp beam.
For clarity, a slightly higher three-quarter view within this final panel is allowed if needed to show both shoulder roots. Keep the pose strong and the body intact.
The empty chest in this panel must also be a genuine through-opening with visible background beyond it, not a closed hangar wall. Remove the departed maintenance cruiser from the waist here as well; it has already exited the frame. The one museum is outside below, the one teal rescue ship still steadies it, and the red escort remains separate. Do not duplicate any ship.

Keep all other successful details and rendering. Preserve the external hostile cannon's identity and do not put a cannon into the allied giant's empty chest. No text, arrows, labels, numbers or watermark.
